# Figure 1

## Getting the data

Processed data are deposited at ArrayExpress, genome assemblies at ENA:

| Data | Accession |
|---|---|
| Single-nucleus RNA-seq | `E-MTAB-17757` |
| Single-nucleus ATAC-seq | `E-MTAB-17776` |
| Genome assemblies | `PRJEB115767` |

Everything except the single-nucleus atlases is committed in this repository
under `data/reference/`: orthology maps, TF lists, SAMap scores, gene-to-GO
maps, TF activity, the differential expression tables and the SCENIC+ output.

Only the atlases need downloading. Put them in one folder and point
`DATA_DIR` at it; the files are used exactly as ArrayExpress delivers them, so
nothing needs renaming.

```
<DATA_DIR>/
`-- snRNA/
    `-- seurat/                                  E-MTAB-17757
        |-- BifurcaAtlas.rds
        |-- BrachiAtlas.rds
        |-- FormosaAtlas.rds
        |-- GracilisAtlas_pregnant_non_pregnant.rds
        |-- GracilisAtlas_pregnant.rds
        |-- InfansAtlas.rds
        |-- PhallocerusAtlas.rds
        |-- PictaAtlas.rds
        |-- ProlificaAtlas.rds
        |-- TurneriAtlas_pregnant_non_pregnant_juvenile.rds
        `-- TurneriAtlas_pregnant.rds
```

Panels use the combined atlas for *P. gracilis* and *P. turneri* unless stated
otherwise; Figure 1B uses the pregnant-only *P. turneri* atlas.

Every atlas carries a `cell_type` column, which the scripts use rather than
per-species cluster numbers.

## Panels in this file

| Panel | Chunk | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 1B | `fig1b` | *P. prolifica* and *P. turneri* UMAPs |
| 1C | `fig1c` | SAMap correlation, *P. prolifica* vs *P. turneri* |
| 1E | `fig1e` | SAMap cell-type tree, five placental species |

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
## PURPOSE : Set the two paths every chunk below reads from, and load packages.
## PRODUCES: DATA_DIR, REF_DIR
## QUESTION: none - configuration only.

DATA_DIR <- "XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX"   # master folder described above
REF_DIR  <- "../data/reference"             # reference tables, committed in this repo

stopifnot(dir.exists(DATA_DIR), dir.exists(REF_DIR))

## The atlases are read under the names ArrayExpress delivers, so nothing needs
## renaming after download.
ATLAS <- c(bifurca   = "BifurcaAtlas.rds",
           brachi    = "BrachiAtlas.rds",
           formosa   = "FormosaAtlas.rds",
           gracilis  = "GracilisAtlas_pregnant_non_pregnant.rds",
           infans    = "InfansAtlas.rds",
           phallo    = "PhallocerusAtlas.rds",
           picta     = "PictaAtlas.rds",
           prolifica = "ProlificaAtlas.rds",
           turneri   = "TurneriAtlas_pregnant_non_pregnant_juvenile.rds")

ATLAS_PREGNANT <- c(gracilis = "GracilisAtlas_pregnant.rds",
                    turneri  = "TurneriAtlas_pregnant.rds")

atlas_path <- function(sp, pregnant = FALSE)
  file.path(DATA_DIR, "snRNA", "seurat",
            if (pregnant) ATLAS_PREGNANT[[sp]] else ATLAS[[sp]])


suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(viridis)
  library(pheatmap)
  library(dendextend)
  library(Seurat)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(patchwork)
})
```

```{r fig1b, fig.width = 12, fig.height = 6}
## PURPOSE : Figure 1B - UMAP of each atlas, coloured by the paper's cell types.
## PRODUCES: the two UMAPs side by side with a shared legend
## QUESTION: which cell types make up the ovary of each placental species, and
##           is the late follicle cell a discrete population in both?

## P. turneri is shown with its pregnant samples only; P. prolifica has a
## single atlas. The combined turneri atlas is used elsewhere in the paper.
## An atlas may carry more than one UMAP. The integrated embedding is the one
## the paper shows, so an "unintegrated" reduction is only used as a fallback -
## picking it by accident is what makes these panels disagree with the figure.
pick_reduction <- function(obj, sp) {
  r <- Reductions(obj)
  message(sp, " reductions: ", paste(r, collapse = ", "))
  umaps <- grep("umap", r, value = TRUE, ignore.case = TRUE)
  if (!length(umaps)) stop(sp, ": no UMAP reduction. Available: ",
                           paste(r, collapse = ", "))
  keep <- umaps[!grepl("unintegrated", umaps, ignore.case = TRUE)]
  out  <- if (length(keep)) keep[1] else umaps[1]
  message(sp, " using reduction: ", out)
  out
}

PANELS <- c(turneri = TRUE, prolifica = FALSE)   # TRUE = use the pregnant-only atlas
objs <- lapply(setNames(names(PANELS), names(PANELS)), function(sp)
  readRDS(atlas_path(sp, pregnant = PANELS[[sp]])))

## one colour per cell type across both panels, so a type reads the same in each
all_types <- sort(unique(unlist(lapply(objs, function(o) as.character(o$cell_type)))))
PAL <- setNames(scales::hue_pal()(length(all_types)), all_types)

umap_panel <- function(sp, label) {
  obj <- objs[[sp]]
  DimPlot(obj, group.by = "cell_type", reduction = pick_reduction(obj, sp),
          cols = PAL, label = FALSE, raster = FALSE) +
    coord_fixed() +
    ggtitle(label) +
    labs(x = "UMAP-1", y = "UMAP-2") +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "italic", hjust = 0.5))
}

(umap_panel("turneri", "P. turneri") | umap_panel("prolifica", "P. prolifica")) +
  plot_layout(guides = "collect") &
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.text = element_text(size = 8))
```


```{r samap-matrix}
## PURPOSE : Read the pairwise SAMap mapping scores for all nine poeciliids.
## PRODUCES: mat - a cluster x cluster matrix of SAMap scores
## QUESTION: how transcriptionally similar is each cell cluster to each cluster
##           in every other species?

mat <- as.matrix(read.csv(
  file.path(REF_DIR, "rna", "SAMap", "MappingValues_Pairwise_samap.txt"),
  row.names = 1))

## The matrix is labelled <two-letter species>_<cluster number>. The cleaned
## atlases no longer carry that clustering, so the cluster -> cell type key is
## committed alongside the matrix; see its `source` column for how each was set.
CLUSTER_KEY <- read.csv(file.path(REF_DIR, "rna", "SAMap", "cluster_cell_types.csv"))
cell_type_of <- setNames(CLUSTER_KEY$cell_type, CLUSTER_KEY$label)

## a species may have more than one cluster of a type, so the cluster is kept
## in the label to keep rows distinguishable and traceable to the matrix
pretty_label <- function(x) ifelse(is.na(cell_type_of[x]), x,
                                   sprintf("%s (%s)", cell_type_of[x], x))

dim(mat)
```

```{r fig1c, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 6}
## PURPOSE : Figure 1C - correlate the P. prolifica and P. turneri clusters
##           through their shared SAMap profiles against all other species.
## PRODUCES: the heatmap, printed in the document
## QUESTION: do two species that evolved placentation independently build their
##           ovaries from matching cell types?

turneri_clusters   <- c("tu_10","tu_3","tu_8","tu_0","tu_1","tu_11","tu_12",
                        "tu_16","tu_2","tu_20","tu_4")
prolifica_clusters <- c("pr_3","pr_17","pr_6","pr_2","pr_4","pr_10","pr_9",
                        "pr_11","pr_12","pr_16","pr_5","pr_13")

## zebrafish columns are the outgroup used to build the scores, not a comparison
tu_mat <- mat[turneri_clusters,   !grepl("^ze_", colnames(mat))]
pr_mat <- mat[prolifica_clusters, !grepl("^ze_", colnames(mat))]

cor_mat <- cor(t(pr_mat), t(tu_mat), use = "pairwise.complete.obs")

rownames(cor_mat) <- pretty_label(rownames(cor_mat))
colnames(cor_mat) <- pretty_label(colnames(cor_mat))

pheatmap(cor_mat,
         color                    = viridis(100),
         cluster_rows             = FALSE,   # order is biological, set above
         cluster_cols             = FALSE,
         main                     = "P. prolifica vs P. turneri",
         angle_col                = 45,
         fontsize = 8, fontsize_row = 8, fontsize_col = 6,
         border_color             = NA)
```

```{r fig1e, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 6}
## PURPOSE : Figure 1E - cluster the five placental species' cell types on
##           1 - Pearson correlation of their SAMap profiles.
## PRODUCES: the dendrogram, printed in the document
## QUESTION: do cell types group by cell type across species, or by species?

placental_clusters <- c(
  "bi_0","bi_2","bi_3","bi_4","bi_6","bi_7","bi_8","bi_12","bi_19",
  "pr_1","pr_3","pr_5","pr_6","pr_8","pr_9","pr_10","pr_12","pr_17",
  "tu_1","tu_2","tu_3","tu_4","tu_5","tu_7","tu_9","tu_10","tu_11","tu_12",
  "fo_0","fo_1","fo_2","fo_5","fo_6","fo_7","fo_8","fo_9","fo_11",
  "ph_0","ph_1","ph_3","ph_4","ph_7","ph_8","ph_10","ph_15")

## subset in the matrix's own order, as Diego's script does - taking them in
## the order of the list above would change how ties are broken in the tree
keep <- rownames(mat)[rownames(mat) %in% placental_clusters]
m    <- mat[keep, keep]

rownames(m) <- colnames(m) <- pretty_label(rownames(m))

d    <- as.dist(1 - cor(t(m), method = "pearson"))
dend <- as.dendrogram(hclust(d, method = "average")) |>
  color_branches(k = 10) |>
  set("labels_cex", 0.7) |>
  set("labels_col", "black")

plot(dend, main = "SAMap cell-type tree, placental species (1 - Pearson)")
```
